The test image shows a tomato leaf with a large, irregular brown-gray lesion surrounded by a pale yellowish-green border. The lesion appears somewhat water-soaked and greasy-looking. This strongly suggests Late Blight, given the characteristic pale green/gray halo around the necrotic tissue.

Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image shows Late Blight sporangia under a microscope (confirming the pathogen identity), but doesn't help with macroscopic comparison. Based on my analysis of the test image:

**Test image features:**
- Large, irregular brown-gray necrotic lesion on a tomato leaf
- Characteristic pale yellowish-green halo/border surrounding the lesion
- Water-soaked, somewhat greasy appearance
- No concentric rings (ruling out Early Blight)
- No small circular spots (ruling out Septoria)
- No fuzzy gray spore masses (ruling out Gray Mold)

This matches Late Blight perfectly: "dead tissue surrounded by a pale green or gray border... lesions appear water-soaked, dark brown, and greasy... leaf lesions surrounded by distinctive pale green or gray halos."
